printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE / NO CHANGE

printableContentReview.wording: Picture your partner’s ideal end to a busy day: quiet company, a long chat or something to laugh at. Choose their answer before asking them.

printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE / NO CHANGE

printableContentReview.wording: Design an imaginary room made for the two of you. Build it aloud in four rounds: comfort, delight, quiet and one impossible feature; spend a little time exploring each other’s additions.

printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE; do not advertise paper as a 15-minute equivalent

printableContentReview.wording: Create the smallest possible celebration using only your hands. Teach it to each other and perform your two versions together.
printableContentReview.problem: Small hand celebration can feel performative or low-value.
printableContentReview.recommendation: Targeted low-pressure review under I02; no automatic replacement

printableContentReview.wording: Make a spoken postcard from tonight: each choose a moment, a detail and a feeling you would put on it. Read your versions to each other and end with one line you would keep.
printableContentReview.problem: Spoken postcard / read your versions ambiguity.
printableContentReview.recommendation: Recommend copy clarification under I11

printableContentReview.wording: Give today a made-up episode title. Trade the story behind your titles, including the detail that would make the trailer.
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Day retelling can drift toward reflection rather than comedy.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE / NO CHANGE

printableContentReview.wording: An imaginary remote can mute hiccups, summon a perfect snack or translate animal thoughts. Which button would your partner press first?
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Absurd remote may feel juvenile to humor-averse couples.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE; intended Funny fit is strong

printableContentReview.wording: Invent a useless household gadget together. Give it a name, a ridiculous feature and a sales pitch delivered by both of you.
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Invent-and-pitch asks for improv energy.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE; central Funny purpose, no blanket removal

printableContentReview.wording: Hold three tiny debates: square pillows versus round pillows, whispering robots versus singing doors, and pockets versus capes. Each gets about a minute to make a case per round; change sides for the last one.
printableContentReview.problem: Three timed debate rounds may drag if the pair dislikes performance.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE; do not force actual timers

printableContentReview.wording: Invent a short sign-off for tonight using a detail you each enjoyed. Trade the stories behind your choices, combine them into one phrase and try it in two ridiculous voices before saying goodbye.
printableContentReview.problem: Ridiculous voices and saying goodbye may feel artificial.
printableContentReview.recommendation: Targeted review under I02; retain an intentional ending

printableContentReview.wording: Trade three tiny details that make you feel drawn to your partner: a look, a habit or a way they do something ordinary. Take turns telling the small story behind each one and leave time to hear what they noticed about you.
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Three attraction details assume comfort giving personal appreciation.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE; marked Flirty and optional participation

printableContentReview.wording: Predict your partner’s favourite kind of anticipation: a playful clue, a direct invitation or a surprise detail. Think of a tasteful example for your guess.
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Anticipation can sound abstract until examples are supplied.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE; current examples reduce ambiguity

printableContentReview.wording: Build a scene with obvious chemistry and no romantic words. Choose a setting, improvise a short exchange, then change who makes the first move in the scene.
printableContentReview.problem: Chemistry acting is a repeated discomfort cluster for P2/P4/P7.
printableContentReview.recommendation: Recommend targeted paper/content review under I02/I03

printableContentReview.wording: Make an everyday phrase sound like an irresistible invitation. Each try “There is a seat here” in two different ways and let your partner choose their favourite.
printableContentReview.problem: Irresistible delivery can feel forced, especially adjacent to the scene.
printableContentReview.recommendation: Recommend targeted review under I03

printableContentReview.wording: Choose one small way to end with a little more spark: a warm compliment, a held gaze or an offered hand. Each suggest your preference and choose an ending you both welcome.
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Held gaze or offered hand needs mutual comfort.
printableContentReview.recommendation: NO CHANGE: prompt already requires an ending both welcome

printableContentReview.wording: Choose one everyday talent you admire in each other. Explain where you would recruit your partner to use it on an imaginary two-person team.
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Imaginary two-person team is more appreciation than rivalry.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE; useful cooperative opening

printableContentReview.wording: In three rounds, predict which your partner would rather master: cooking or storytelling, fixing things or finding things, planning or improvising. Give a reason for each guess.
printableContentReview.problem: Preference pairs are generic; demonstrating skills may suggest props.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE and test comprehension before a wording change

printableContentReview.wording: Solve a mystery you invent together: why is there a tiny door behind the sofa? Alternate adding clues, discuss two possible explanations and agree on a final reveal.
printableContentReview.problem: An invented mystery has no authored solution or measurable win.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE under I04; do not add scoring

printableContentReview.wording: Build a sound sequence together: one person makes a sound, the other repeats it and adds one. Keep extending it at an easy pace, then try a second sequence with roles reversed.
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Sound memory is a familiar mechanic and may exclude a quiet preference.
printableContentReview.recommendation: OBSERVE; natural turn-taking is a strength

printableContentReview.wording: Each offer one tiny, no-cost date you could share at home another time. Pick the idea you are both most curious about and end by inviting each other to it.
printableContentReview.problem: No material defect observed. Preference boundary: Future invitation is simple rather than a competitive finale.
printableContentReview.recommendation: NO CHANGE: closure should soften rivalry, not crown a winner
